A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EgoAgent with matching authors, architecture and core experiments. Text extraction and visual inspection cover both complete documents, including supplementary material, allowing content to be matched across renaming, relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, future-state retrieval, human-motion prediction and ablation results in Tables 1–4, plus TriFinger simulation results in supplementary Table 5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experimental and simulation results and adds baseline evaluations, ablations and qualitative analyses in the main text and supplement.

M1.justification: The InternLM backbone, continuous image/action tokens, interleaved queries, asymmetric EMA branches and three losses remain unchanged, as do the supplementary architecture configurations. Predictor/observer replaces student/teacher terminology; the expanded causal-attention explanation does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions cover WalkingTours, Ego-Exo4D, ImageNet-100/1K and TriFinger reach/move-cube tasks. TriFinger moves from v1 supplementary Section 6 into v2 Section 4.4. The new pose-conditioning and attention analyses probe retained tasks without establishing additional dataset, population or domain coverage.

E2.justification: V2 adds a DoRA variant trained on WT+Ego-Exo4D to retrieval, classification and TriFinger comparisons, and removes the DoRA WT-Venice variant from TriFinger. OpenSora disappears from the direct classification comparison, although its supplementary classification analysis and qualitative video comparisons remain. Other comparator families are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds matched-training-data DoRA comparisons and additional task/loss controls while retaining the main splits, metrics and budgets. Motion-test inputs change in the description from four images to five, and Diffusion Policy explicitly receives five past poses alongside images. Retrieval-gallery wording changes from next-frame features to all video frames. These are reported protocol revisions; unchanged scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's leave-one-task-out and VQGAN analyses, v2 Table 3 adds three single-task experiments and a VQGAN variant including representation supervision. Main Figure 4 tests different poses with a fixed observation, and supplementary Figure 4 examines task-dependent attention. These substantially extend evidence about task interactions and action conditioning. Existing OpenSora and subtle-motion analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for its experimental results. Additional result rows do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Retained EgoAgent benchmark scores are unchanged, but v2 adds substantial control findings and combined-data DoRA results. For example, action-only training gives 14.32 MPJPE and 91.13 MPJVE versus joint training's 14.49 and 88.61. DINO ImageNet-1K Top1 changes from 31.1 to 22.18 with training now labeled WT-Venice, so a same-setting decline is not established. The DoRA-Venice TriFinger row, OpenSora ImageNet-1K scores and numerical results for ablated-away tasks are omitted.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4 retain the same losses and combined objective. Branch names and temporal notation change without substantive mathematical revisions. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs; the added cognitive and causal discussion is conceptual.

C1.justification: The central claim of jointly learning representation, state prediction and action prediction remains. V2 strengthens novelty by calling EgoAgent the first such agent model in a unified representation and explicitly presenting causal interleaving and temporal asymmetric JEAP branches as two innovations. The highlighted TriFinger capability was already reported in v1's supplement.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands interpretation: it attributes combined-data DoRA degradation to tracking difficulties, explains task dependencies and noisy supervision, and discusses the position-error versus motion-smoothness tradeoff revealed by single-task training. It also interprets pose-conditioned retrieval and attention shifts as evidence of action-sensitive understanding. V1's finger-detail and long-term-memory limitations remain recognizable as future-work directions.

D1.justification: V2 Table 1 clarifies official-checkpoint use for representation baselines and training from scratch for motion baselines, and specifies DINO's WT-Venice training source. It removes the main-text Adam wording that conflicted with v1's supplementary AdamW table. Architecture tables, hyperparameters, preprocessing, hardware, training times and the promised code/model release remain essentially unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 substantially reframes the motivation around embodied cognition and Common Coding Theory, adding works by Barsalou, Prinz, Shapiro and Spaulding, and Thelen and Smith. It positions EgoAgent explicitly as an extension of JEPA from world modeling to agent modeling, strengthens the novelty claim, adds visual sequential-modeling literature and removes several general LLM and scene-aware motion citations.

P1.justification: The title is shortened, and the abstract, introduction, related work and method explanation are extensively rewritten. Related-work topics and experimental tasks are reordered; architecture and training explanations are reorganized; student/teacher terminology becomes predictor/observer. TriFinger enters the main narrative, and the supplement receives independent numbering and references.

P2.justification: V1 Tables 1–3 become one cross-task table in v2; the TriFinger table moves into the main paper; and the ablation table gains rows and reorganized columns. Retrieval and motion figures are resized or redesigned, and new pose-conditioning and attention figures are added. These materially change the visual organization beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2's VQGAN control with representation supervision addresses a confound in v1's feature-space comparison, while single-task and same-data DoRA controls strengthen the joint-learning argument. Reorganization also clarifies the unchanged method. The gain is limited by reporting inconsistencies: motion-input descriptions change despite identical scores, and the retained TriFinger +3.90-point claim depends on the DoRA-Venice result removed from v2's table.
